articles.headline: Staircase Sprints Beat the Gym: Tiny Workout Bursts Win Big
articles.body: Forget lengthy gym sessions. <cite index="46-7">Just 3–4 one-minute vigorous bursts daily are associated with 25–30% lower all-cause mortality and approximately 40% lower cardiovascular mortality.</cite> These "exercise snacks"—brief, intense movements like stair sprinting or explosive squats scattered throughout your day—deliver fitness gains that rival traditional workouts. <cite index="45-3">Accumulating roughly 11-12 minutes of intense, brief physical activity daily, distributed naturally throughout your day, appears sufficient to substantially reduce cardiovascular disease risk.</cite> Perfect for busy parents and professionals. No special equipment needed.
articles.takeaway: Three or four one-minute bursts of intense movement daily—stairs, sprints, anything that gets you breathless—deliver measurable cardiovascular benefits. No gym membership required.
articles.source: Frontiers in Public Health, UK Biobank data, FoundMyFitness

articles.headline: One Dose. 48 Hours. Depression Symptoms Shift
articles.body: <cite index="48-2,48-3">A single dose of psilocybin produced rapid improvements in depression symptoms in a small Swedish clinical trial, published in JAMA Network Open.</cite> <cite index="48-7">Eight days after treatment, depression scores had fallen by an average of 9.7 points in the psilocybin group, compared with 2.4 points in the placebo group.</cite> Most striking: <cite index="49-5">six weeks after the study, 53% of participants who received psilocybin reported they were in remission, compared to just 6% from the control group.</cite> This challenges conventional depression treatment timelines. Researchers are investigating how this single intervention reshapes brain chemistry.
articles.takeaway: A single therapeutic dose of psilocybin produced clinically meaningful depression relief within days, with remission rates significantly higher than placebo at 6 weeks.

articles.topic: Parkinson's exercise slows cognitive decline progression
articles.headline: Movement Is Medicine: Exercise Blocks Parkinson's Cognitive Decline
articles.body: <cite index="57-2,57-3">At least 4 hours of moderate-to-vigorous exercise weekly was associated with slower cognition and motor decline over years of follow up in patients with mild-to-moderate Parkinson's disease.</cite> <cite index="63-5,63-6">The least active group experienced an annual average drop in cognitive scores of 0.478 points, while the most active participants reported a remarkable average decrease of just 0.007 points, suggesting their cognitive function remained nearly stable.</cite> <cite index="57-7">Physical activity appears to provide dual clinical benefits by independently reducing both motor progression and cognitive decline.</cite> Consistency matters more than intensity.
articles.takeaway: Adults with Parkinson's who stay physically active experience dramatically slower cognitive decline—the most active group's memory and thinking abilities remained nearly stable while inactive individuals declined sharply.

articles.topic: Deep sleep growth hormone muscle repair recovery
articles.headline: Your Brain Rewires Growth: How Deep Sleep Builds Muscle and Clears Toxins
articles.body: <cite index="20-2,20-3">Researchers have identified the brain circuitry that links deep sleep with the release of growth hormone, revealing how the two regulate each other. The newly discovered feedback loop helps explain why poor sleep can interfere with growth, muscle repair, fat metabolism, and brain function.</cite> <cite index="20-4">Sleep stimulates growth hormone production, but growth hormone also sends signals back to the brain that influence when we wake up.</cite> This two-way communication is essential. <cite index="23-8,23-9">During NREM sleep, the brain performs essential maintenance functions that support learning, memory, and recovery. Deep sleep is also associated with processes that help clear metabolic waste products from the brain.</cite>
articles.takeaway: Deep sleep and growth hormone form a feedback loop that controls muscle repair, fat metabolism, and brain cleanup. This reciprocal system is why consistent, quality sleep is non-negotiable for recovery.

workout.title: Steady State Foundation: 40-Minute Conversational Base Run
workout.tip: If you can't say a full sentence, you're too fast. Zone 2 feels *easy*—embrace the lack of urgency. This builds the aerobic engine that makes race paces feel sustainable.
workout.warmup: 5 min easy jog + 3 × 20 sec dynamic leg swings (forward/back, side-to-side), 10 walking lunges

exercises.name: Continuous Zone 2 Run
exercises.notes: Maintain conversational pace (120–140 bpm estimated). Focus on nasal breathing when possible; if mouth breathing becomes necessary, you're above Z2. Cadence should feel relaxed, around 170–180 steps per minute. This is aerobic base work—no speed goals, only consistency.

workout.cooldown: 3 min easy walking + standing quad stretch 30 sec each leg, forward fold 45 sec, calf stretch 30 sec each leg
workout.description: A pure Zone 2 aerobic run at conversational pace—the cornerstone of endurance fitness for 5K, 10K, half-marathon, and marathon athletes. This "boring" work builds aerobic capacity, improves fat oxidation, and accelerates recovery between harder sessions. Intermediate runners will target 120–140 bpm (or a pace where you can speak in full sentences) for the entire 40 minutes.

meal.title: Roasted Chickpea & Rosemary Cluster
meal.description: A crunchy, herb-forward snack with plant-based protein and fiber—great for general fitness athletes seeking a savory alternative to typical processed snacks.
ingredients: 1 can (400g) chickpeas, drained and patted dry
meal.instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
2. Toss drained chickpeas with olive oil, rosemary, salt, and pepper.
3. Spread on a sheet pan in a single layer.
4. Roast for 25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until golden and crispy.
5. Cool slightly before eating; they'll continue to crisp up as they cool.
meal.tip: Make a batch on Sunday and store in an airtight container for up to 4 days—perfect for grab-and-go all week.
